canonical_name: Adversarial NLI (ANLI), rounds A1-A3 (Nie et al., Facebook AI / UNC)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.14599 (v1 31 Oct 2019); data v0.1 committed to https://github.com/facebookresearch/anli on 2019-11-01
metric: Accuracy (3-way NLI) on test rounds A1 (1,000), A2 (1,000), A3 (1,200); reported per round and combined
abandoned_evidence: Last 9-lab report: PaLM 2 technical report (Google, 2023-05-17, ANLI R1 73.1); none after per lab_reports. Official leaderboard = GitHub README of facebookresearch/anli, last leaderboard commit 2021-01-22 ('Leaderboard with Boxin's numbers'), later README commits only docs (last 2022-05-12). >= 12 months without either by 2024-05.
score_at_release_system: RoBERTa-Large trained on SNLI+MNLI+FEVER+ANLI (combined test; A1 73.8 / A2 48.9 / A3 44.4)
n_items: 3,200 test (A1 1,000; A2 1,000; A3 1,200); dev same sizes; train ~163k
lineage: Human-and-model-in-the-loop successor to SNLI/MNLI/FEVER-NLI; precursor of Dynabench (2020-09); not to be confused with AI2's alpha-NLI ('anli') leaderboard
best_by_cutoff: Per round, best found: A1 78.7 (PaLM-540B prompt-order rationale-augmented ensemble, test, arXiv 2207.00747, 2022-07); A3 74.7 (ST-MoE-32B fine-tuned, arXiv 2202.08906, 2022-02); A2 66.5 / A3 67.9 (PaLM-540B LMSI + self-consistency, arXiv 2210.11610, 2022-10). GitHub leaderboard best: InfoBERT A1 75.5; ALBERT A2 58.6, A3 53.4
notes: No human accuracy reported by the creators (only verifier agreement during collection) -> criterion B (90). No result >= 90 on any round found by 2026-09-30, so no AB/strict event. Unit treated at the whole-benchmark level; labs report single rounds (R1 or R3). Abandonment judgement: there was also a quiet spell 2021-01 (last leaderboard edit) to 2021-09 (Google FLAN paper evaluates ANLI) - < 12 months once Google research papers are counted; terminal silence starts after PaLM 2 (2023-05). If only model-release materials in lab_reports count, an earlier >= 12-month gap exists (2021-01-22 to PaLM 2022-04-05) - flagged for adjudication. The AI2 leaderboard named 'anli' is abductive NLI (alpha-NLI), not this benchmark.

Backward search: AI2 leaderboard never had an entry >= 0.90 (top ST-MoE-32B 0.8652 in captures up to 2025-05/06); ST-MoE paper (2022-02) lists previous best 81.4; LMSI (PaLM 540B self-improve + self-consistency 32 paths, arXiv 2210.11610, 2022-10) 89.8, previous SOTA 88.7 (self-consistency 2022-03) -> all below 90. C event = platform-wide AI2 leaderboard freeze (coded literally; judgement call). Scores are format-sensitive (separate-option scoring gives much lower numbers, e.g., LLaMA 65B 56.0 0-shot). Strict caveat: competitor columns in other labs' launch materials (e.g., Llama 3 launch post 2024-04-18, image tables) and OpenCompass-style 2023 evaluations could hold earlier independent runs >= 90 but could not be verified; strict date is the earliest verified.

canonical_name: The Belebele Benchmark: a parallel reading comprehension dataset in 122 language variants (Bandarkar et al., Meta AI)
metric: Accuracy (4-way multiple choice), averaged over the 122 language variants (900 questions each)
abandoned_evidence: Only Qwen reports it among the 9 labs; last report Qwen3 technical report (arXiv 2505.09388, 2025-05-14, 80 of 122 languages, Table 36/37); no later 9-lab report found (DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K2 tables checked: absent). No official leaderboard exists (GitHub repo only).
score_at_release_system: XLM-V large, translate-train-all fine-tuning (average over 122 variants); best LLM: GPT3.5-turbo zero-shot 51.1 avg; Llama 2 70B 5-shot 48.0 avg but 90.9 on English
n_items: 900 questions x 122 language variants = 109,800 items (test-only dataset)
lineage: Passages from FLORES-200 (2022); arXiv v2 2024-07; later multilingual suites (e.g., Global-MMLU, Global PIQA) are separate benchmarks
best_by_cutoff: No full-122-language average >= 90 found. Best documented: Qwen3-32B (Thinking) on 80 languages by family, e.g., Indo-European 90.7, Sino-Tibetan 89.7, Uralic 91.3, Afro-Asiatic 84.8 (Qwen3 report Table 37, 2025-05; self-report). English alone: Llama 2 70B 5-shot 90.9 already at release
notes: Human 97.6 = mean of 4 authors each answering ~30 English questions (English only, not the multilingual test) -> not 'same split' -> criterion B (90) on the cross-language average. If the unit were scored on English only, it would be born saturated (Llama 2 70B 90.9 at release). Labs report non-standard subsets (Qwen1.5/2/2.5: 12 languages inside an aggregate 'Multi-Understanding' score; Qwen3: 80 languages), so the official all-language average is rarely reported; web-search budget was exhausted, so third-party (non-lab) evaluations of frontier models on all 122 variants could not be checked - an AB event in 2024-2026 cannot be excluded (low confidence). Abandonment date = last 9-lab report (2025-05).

canonical_name: BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions (Clark et al.)
metric: Accuracy (yes/no), hidden test set scored via the SuperGLUE evaluation server
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683v1 (T5 v1, 23 Oct 2019, Table 14: BoolQ test accuracy T5-11B 91.0, previous best 87.1; later versions report 91.2)
strict_system: T5-11B single model, scored by SuperGLUE evaluation server (organizers)
score_at_release_system: BERT-large pre-trained on MultiNLI then fine-tuned on BoolQ (authors), test accuracy
n_items: ~3.2k test (labels hidden; SuperGLUE server); ~3.2k dev; ~9.4k train (16k questions total)
lineage: Built from Natural Questions-style Google queries; incorporated into SuperGLUE (2019-05); no direct successor
best_by_cutoff: 92.4 test, ST-MoE-32B (Google, arXiv 2202.08906, 2022-02); LLM self-reports on dev: PaLM 2-L 90.9 (1-shot, 2023-05), PaLM 540B 89.1 (few-shot, 2022-04)
notes: Human 90% = three authors labelled 110 random examples and resolved disagreements by mutual agreement (consensus label, not the test split) -> treated as aggregate -> criterion B; threshold is 90 under either reading. SuperGLUE's separate crowd baseline for BoolQ is 89.0 (majority vote). Previous best on test before T5 was RoBERTa 87.1 (SuperGLUE, 2019-07); T5-3B 89.9 just below threshold. SuperGLUE leaderboard UI/API not retrievable from the Wayback Machine (React app), so date rests on T5 arXiv v1 (submission also on SuperGLUE leaderboard in Oct 2019). curation 'mined' = naturally occurring search queries paired with Wikipedia passages, labelled by annotators. format coded multiple-choice (binary yes/no).

canonical_name: CoQA: A Conversational Question Answering Challenge (Reddy, Chen & Manning)

ab_source: https://github.com/stanfordnlp/coqa/blob/gh-pages/index.html (gh-pages commit of 2019-03-29 adds entry dated 'Mar 29, 2019', in-domain 89.9 / out-of-domain 88.0 / overall 89.4); live page https://stanfordnlp.github.io/coqa/

strict_source: https://github.com/stanfordnlp/coqa/blob/gh-pages/index.html (first appears in gh-pages commit of 2019-09-11, entry dated 'Sep 05, 2019'); paper https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.10772

lineage: No official parent/successor; contemporaneous sibling QuAC (2018-08); later absorbed into LLM eval suites (GPT-2/GPT-3/PaLM dev-set reports)

Before 2019-03-29 the best was BERT+MMFT+ADA (ensemble) 86.8 (2019-01-25). canonical_name: CommonsenseQA (Talmor et al.), v1.11 random split
metric: Accuracy (5-way multiple choice), hidden test set via leaderboard (random split)
abandoned_evidence: Last lab report: Meta Llama 3.1 model card (2024-07-23, 7-shot 85.8, dev); no report by the 9 labs in the 26 months to 2026-09-30 (per lab_reports). Official test leaderboard (tau-nlp.sites.tau.ac.il/csqa-leaderboard, 'Version 1.11') shows no documented new test entries after KEAR (Nov 2021); PwC test listing tops at KEAR 89.4 (https://www.sota2.com/research/sota/commonsense-reasoning-on-csqa-test).
n_items: 12,102 questions (v1.11), 80/10/10 split -> ~1.1k test (labels hidden), ~1.2k dev, ~9.7k train
lineage: Questions seeded from ConceptNet; successors CommonsenseQA 2.0 (arXiv 2201.05320, 2022-01) and multilingual X-CSQA (2021)
best_by_cutoff: Test: 89.4, KEAR ensemble of 39 models (Microsoft), leaderboard Nov 2021 (blog 2021-12-20 https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/azure-ai-milestone-microsoft-kear-surpasses-human-performance-on-commonsenseqa-benchmark/). Dev-set reports above 90 exist but do not count: PaLM 2-L 90.4 (7-shot CoT + self-consistency, 2023-05, compared against KEAR dev 91.2), KEAR ensemble dev 93.4
notes: Human 88.9 = majority vote of five workers on 100 random questions -> aggregate -> criterion B (90). No result >= 90 on the official hidden test split found (best 89.4). Under criterion A (88.9) the event would be KEAR ensemble 89.4 on the test leaderboard (Nov 2021; arXiv 2112.03254 v1 6 Dec 2021; strict-eligible single model 86.1 never crossed). LLM numbers (PaLM 2 90.4 etc.) are dev-set and excluded by the official-test-split rule - if dev results were admitted, AB would be 2023-05 (PaLM 2). The Wix-hosted leaderboard table could not be extracted from Wayback captures, so later test entries cannot be fully excluded. CSQA 2.0 paper speaks of benchmarks reaching human parity in general but does not name CSQA v1 saturation as reason -> no C. Abandonment: 9-lab reporting stopped after 2024-07 and no leaderboard activity documented since 2021.

canonical_name: GLUE: General Language Understanding Evaluation benchmark (Wang et al.)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07461 (v1 20 Apr 2018; leaderboard gluebenchmark.com launched with the paper)
metric: GLUE score = macro-average of 9 task test metrics (evaluation server)
ab_source: https://syncedreview.com/2019/12/11/baidus-pre-training-model-ernie-achieves-new-nlp-benchmark-record/ ('world's first model to score over 90 ... (90.1)', 2019-12-11); https://www.technologyreview.com/2019/12/26/131372/ai-baidu-ernie-google-bert-natural-language-glue/ ('first team to surpass 90')
strict_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683 (Table 14 in v3 of 28 Jul 2020 / ar5iv: GLUE Average 90.3 test); in late 2019 T5's leaderboard score was 89.7 (SMART paper table, https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03437)
c_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.00537v1 (SuperGLUE v1, 2 May 2019, by the GLUE creators)
c_quote: performance on the benchmark has recently come close to the level of non-expert humans, suggesting limited headroom for further research. This paper recaps lessons learned from the GLUE benchmark and presents SuperGLUE
score_at_release_system: Single-task BiLSTM + ELMo (authors' baseline), v1 Table 5 Avg (best multi-task/sentence-encoder baseline GenSen 59.2)
n_items: 9 task test sets (~430k test examples in total, dominated by QQP ~391k; CoLA 1.1k, SST-2 1.8k, MRPC 1.7k, STS-B 1.4k, MNLI ~20k, QNLI, RTE 3k, WNLI 146) + AX diagnostic set
lineage: Aggregates 9 earlier datasets (2005-2018); successor SuperGLUE (2019-05, explicitly motivated by GLUE headroom); many language-specific clones (CLUE, Russian SuperGLUE, etc.)
best_by_cutoff: 91.3 GLUE score: Microsoft Turing ULR v6 (single model, announced 2022-10-31, https://blogs.bing.com/search-quality-insights/october-2022/Microsoft-Turing-Universal-Language-Representation-model,-T-ULRv6,-tops-both-XTREME-and-GLUE-leaderb) and JD Vega v1, per leaderboard scrape https://huggingface.co/spaces/bdx33/GLUE-leaderboard
notes: Human baseline 87.1 (Nangia & Bowman 2019, GLUE team) = majority vote of five trained crowdworkers -> aggregate -> criterion B (90). Under A (87.1) the crossing happened before 2019-07 (SuperGLUE v2 abstract of 12 Jul 2019 says GLUE performance 'has recently surpassed the level of non-expert humans'; MT-DNN ensemble 87.6 is the likely first, not verified). Primary event is C (2019-05): the GLUE creators' SuperGLUE paper names the lack of headroom on GLUE as the reason for the new benchmark. AB: Baidu ERNIE 90.1 (2019-12) reported as the first GLUE score above 90; T5's leaderboard score was 89.7 (single) and MT-DNN-SMART 89.9 at that time (SMART paper table) - T5 paper's later 90.3 comes from an updated submission. GLUE leaderboard UI/API not captured usefully by the Wayback Machine, so dates rely on press and papers (hence medium confidence). Strict date is an upper bound (T5 v3), earlier single-model >=90 entries cannot be excluded. Lab reports list sub-tasks (SST-2, QNLI) - unit coded at the GLUE-score level.

canonical_name: LAMBADA: word prediction requiring a broad discourse context (Paperno et al.)
metric: Accuracy of predicting the passage-final target word (test set); perplexity secondary
abandoned_evidence: Last 9-lab mention: GPT-4o System Card (OpenAI, 2024-08-08), audio-input variant only; last standard text report Qwen technical report (2023-09-28, 71.1). No official leaderboard; Papers with Code listing (capture 2024-04-24) has no entries newer than 2023-06 (LLaMA+CFG). >= 12 months with no reports/leaderboard activity before 2026-09-30.
score_at_release_system: Heuristic baseline 'random capitalized word from passage'; best language model (N-gram, N-gram w/ cache) 0.1% accuracy
n_items: 5,153 test passages; 4,869 dev passages (10,022 total, from disjoint novels); training corpus of novels
lineage: Drawn from BookCorpus novels with human filtering; OpenAI-detokenized variant ('LAMBADA (OpenAI)') used by GPT-2/GPT-3 and the EleutherAI harness; multilingual translations later (not official)
best_by_cutoff: 89.7, PaLM 540B few-shot (Google, arXiv 2204.02311, 2022-04-05); next PaLM 2-L 86.9 one-shot (2023-05), GPT-3 175B few-shot 86.4 (2020-05) - Papers with Code listing, capture 2024-04-24 (https://web.archive.org/web/20240424091511/https://paperswithcode.com/sota/language-modelling-on-lambada)

(2020-05) 87.7; XTREME leaderboard 'Anonymous1' (Jun 17 2020) sentence-pair avg 83.9 (implies PAWS-X < 90 given XNLI ~80).
